rationale: The gate's central purpose is to restore explicitly supplied system-property precedence over environment values. The repaired commit is titled 'SOLR-18630: preserve system property precedence'; its production comment states that system properties take precedence over environment values, and it adds the directly corresponding test legacyWaitForZkSystemPropertyWinsOverLegacyEnvironment with expected value 5.

The gate explicitly scopes the earlier mixed-source discriminator as previous=5 and new=1, demonstrating that the two-head comparison is meant to distinguish pre-repair from repaired behavior rather than impose one invariant value across both revisions. The additional case is written as an unqualified => 5 and follows the repaired-head acceptance criteria; it is best read as the repaired behavior expectation, not a requirement that the old head already implement the fix.

The previous-head run used its own classpath and loaded EnvUtils from the previous checkout; its raw case log shows -DwaitForZk=5, SOLR_WAIT_FOR_ZK=1, RESULT=1 and process exit 0. The repaired-head log shows the same inputs, RESULT=5 and process exit 0 from the repaired checkout. These are observed values, not predictions.

The prior comparison harness applied 5 to the disputed previous-head case and therefore returned aggregate exit 1. Its only mismatch was this value; all six individual JVM invocations exited 0. With the expected old behavior correctly interpreted as 1, this is not a behavioral failure of the repair gate and no rerun is needed.

conclusion: The existing evidence is sufficient. The prior job's incomplete verdict is left intact as a historical record; this successor resolves its one ambiguity and passes the adjudicated repair gate at head a4ce0580ad89ad521a5402e383d96c239cea94fd.
